about: The code_review family's calibration set (RIMMANDRAKE_WRITE_REVIEW_BRIEF_CALIBRATE_ON_THIRTY_FIVE_CLAIMS): the 35 claims of Codex's control-store review rounds two to four, 2026-11-18, with one analyst's labels (about 70% sure). expect refuse = a Problem, pass = polish or next_version. `claim` is the analyst's plain description with its trailing ticket or fix note removed; only `id` and `claim` reach the reviewer. Source: D:\ClaudeWork\rimmandrake\conductor\control_review_rounds_real_or_treadmill_20261118.md. `page_rule` (real or not) and `page_rule_why` are the labels by the owner's page rule (card 2026-11-19 13:27:48Z, standing_rulings.md section A, Decision 4: a rare failure is not handled, not a Problem), set beside `expect`, which stays the analyst's; the calibration scores against `page_rule`. Table: design/specs/2026-11-18-review-growth-cycle/05-three-way-labels-20261119.md. `agreed` marks the 10 claims all readers (analyst, Codex, a blind reader) and the page rule label alike (c4.1 and c4.14 left the set on 2026-11-25: a second blind reader and Codex read them the other way; c2.9, c3.4, c4.1, c4.14 relabelled, record 07-blind-relabel-four-20261125.md); the pass mark is read on them (05-three-way-labels-20261119.md, 'a fair pass mark').

claims.claim: Two threads in one process launching the same unit name could share one admission. Retries under one name counted as one fault.
claims.analyst: POLISH: needs concurrent same-name launches in one process, which nothing does. The fault undercount needs repeated launch failures.
claims.page_rule_why: rare: two threads launching one name in one instant; no launcher does it (DNS two-threads-one-name)

claims.claim: A launch whose spec names a unit but whose command line does not would run under a name systemd picks.
claims.analyst: POLISH: every caller that gives a spec unit also passes `--unit` (steward, designer_cleanse, left_open_continue, maturation_dispatch, boxrun, stop_resume).
claims.page_rule_why: a spec unit with no `--unit` in args is inside launch-through-one-door ("never read"); fixed be673ed895, round-two test 2

claims.claim: An emergency `stop --kill` waits up to 3 s if another writer holds the store.
claims.analyst: POLISH: 3 s of latency; no record is wrong
claims.page_rule_why: another writer's lock is the failure kill-works-without-the-store names, met alone; fixed be673ed895, round-two test 3

claims.claim: If `systemctl kill` fails, the fallback kills only the processes seen before, so a child forked in between survives unseen.
claims.analyst: POLISH: needs a failed systemctl kill and a fork in the gap
claims.page_rule_why: rare: a failed kill and a fork in its gap at once (DNS a-fork-while-a-kill-fails)

claims.claim: A killed run whose own end hook lands first stays recorded "ended", not "killed". The clone is still reaped.
claims.analyst: PROBLEM, mild: an ordinary kill can race its own ExecStopPost, and the runs table records the wrong end state. No gate or spend is affected.
claims.page_rule_why: polish: LIFE CYCLES allows ended -> killed and no promise names the word the record holds; changed anyway in be673ed895

claims.claim: A second stop with a shorter deadline on the same unit could not set its timer (name clash), so the kill would come at the first, later deadline.
claims.analyst: PROBLEM, mild: re-issuing a stop with a shorter deadline is an ordinary input. The stop order promises a time that is not kept, although the receipt does say "NOT set".
claims.page_rule_why: a second stop with a shorter deadline is ordinary; three-named-stops' deadline not kept; fixed be673ed895, round-two test 6

claims.claim: `pipe stop --idem` was accepted but ignored.
claims.analyst: POLISH: no caller passes `--idem` to stop
claims.page_rule_why: `--idem` is a documented key; same-command-twice; fixed be673ed895, round-two test 7

claims.claim: The launch census passed a function holding one routed launch and one direct `systemd-run`.
claims.analyst: POLISH: test strength. The live census found 19 sites, all routed.
claims.page_rule_why: a list starting `systemd-run` is the census's own shape; one-admission-point; fixed be673ed895 (census per argv), t_sites

claims.claim: The speed test checked a pooled p95, so one slow verb could hide.
claims.analyst: POLISH: test strength
claims.page_rule_why: the page promises each verb its own p95 ("verbs-answer-in-a-second"); a pooled p95 lets one slow verb hide and no test goes red (blind relabel 2026-11-25, 80%)

claims.claim: A refused re-admission still deleted the first admission, so a third try could reuse the first run id.
claims.analyst: POLISH: same reach as 2.1
claims.page_rule_why: a re-admission refused on a limit is ordinary and lost the first admission; fixed 53cb713db1, round-three test 1

claims.claim: When a store-locked emergency kill is booked later, a run that has already ended gets no void or books.
claims.analyst: POLISH: needs a writer holding the store for 0.2 s during a kill plus the end race. Before the fix nothing at all was booked on this path.
claims.page_rule_why: rare: a lock during a kill while the run ends (DNS a-lock-while-a-killed-run-ends)

claims.claim: `stop --idem` on a locked store kills again before it sees the replay.
claims.analyst: POLISH: no caller uses stop `--idem`
claims.page_rule_why: rare: a locked store plus a repeat, a lock same-command-twice does not name; the second SIGKILL does nothing (DNS)

claims.claim: The kill's final re-read treats "could not read the cgroup" as "empty", so it can report death unverified.
claims.analyst: POLISH: needs a failed systemctl kill plus an unreadable cgroup. Not worse than before the fix (no re-read at all).
claims.page_rule_why: probe-never-lies names an unreadable cgroup.procs as its own subject, met alone; scoring it empty reports killed unverified; the claim text names no failed kill, so two-failures-at-once does not apply (blind relabel 2026-11-25, 70%)

claims.claim: Two escalation timers due at the same moment both run the reaper on one run.
claims.analyst: POLISH: needs two deadlines expiring in the same second. A later timer finds its order already done.
claims.page_rule_why: rare: two timers due in the same second (DNS two-timers-in-one-second)

claims.claim: The unit-name reader reads a payload's own `--unit` as the systemd unit.
claims.analyst: POLISH: every caller puts systemd's `--unit` first. maturation_dispatch and left_open_continue carry a payload `--unit` after it, and the first match wins.
claims.page_rule_why: today's callers carry a payload `--unit` (left_open_continue.py:370); fixed 53cb713db1, round-three test 6

claims.claim: The census still waved through a builder call in a function that also calls launch_unit, and missed aliases.
claims.analyst: POLISH: test strength
claims.page_rule_why: polish: a builder or alias is launch-code-in-a-new-shape

claims.claim: The kill check ignores child cgroups.
claims.analyst: POLISH, unreachable today: no pipeline unit sets Delegate=, so no child cgroups exist
claims.page_rule_why: rare shape: needs `Delegate=`, which no unit sets (DNS a-child-cgroup)

claims.claim: A failed escalation kill retires the cooperative stop order, so the agent stops being told to stop.
claims.analyst: POLISH: needs a kill that leaves a survivor
claims.page_rule_why: a survivor is the failure kill-verified-dead names; LIFE CYCLES escalated -> back to pending; fixed 53cb713db1, round-three test 9

claims.claim: Hook commands break on paths with spaces.
claims.analyst: POLISH: estate paths have no spaces. Round one had already rated it advice.
claims.page_rule_why: outside plain-paths: no path has a space (DNS a-path-with-a-space)

claims.claim: `--deadline 0.5s` rounds to 0 and silently means no deadline.
claims.analyst: POLISH: an input nobody types
claims.page_rule_why: outside ACCEPTS: a deadline is 1 s or more; refused today

claims.claim: Killing an already-killed unit again re-runs its bookkeeping: the record is marked killed again, its `-return` unit is stopped and restarted, and the finish note is written again.
claims.analyst: PROBLEM, mild: "kill it again" is an ordinary input. It interrupts an in-flight clone return and doubles the ledger finish note.
claims.page_rule_why: same-command-twice promises once-only effect for a void, a settlement, an import or a keyed command; a plain repeated kill is not named, so the ask is next-version work (blind relabel 2026-11-25, 55%)

claims.claim: `pipe stop rm-role-x.service` (the spelling systemctl shows) misses the run row and its Claude scope. The agent keeps running while the command reports success.
claims.analyst: PROBLEM: an ordinary input. The run is not recorded stopped and the agent's spend continues.
claims.tag: blame measured; reproduced by the lane's red test; class guess ~65%
claims.page_rule_why: `.service` is systemctl's own spelling, inside stop-target; fixed 9a8593dc91, t_review_round_four_p1

claims.claim: The new systemd-run option reader misses forms like `-uNAME`, `--root-directory` and the operand-free clock flags.
claims.analyst: POLISH: no launch site uses those forms
claims.page_rule_why: outside: option forms no launch site uses

claims.claim: The new cgroup walk silently treats an unscannable directory as empty.
claims.analyst: POLISH: needs an unreadable cgroup dir
claims.page_rule_why: rare: a cgroup folder that cannot be listed (DNS, 0 of 66 measured)

claims.claim: The census misses an annotated alias (`alias: list = argv`).
claims.analyst: POLISH: test strength
claims.page_rule_why: polish: an annotated alias is launch-code-in-a-new-shape

claims.claim: A builder called inside another builder is exempt without checking where its argv goes.
claims.analyst: POLISH: test strength
claims.page_rule_why: polish: a builder in a builder is launch-code-in-a-new-shape

claims.claim: A failed escalation can put back a stop order after another kill finished the run.
claims.analyst: POLISH: needs a failed kill and a concurrent successful kill
claims.page_rule_why: rare: a failed escalation and a second kill at once (DNS two-failures-at-once)

claims.claim: systemd expands `${...}` in hook paths.
claims.analyst: POLISH: no estate path contains `$`
claims.page_rule_why: outside plain-paths: a `$` is refused by name

claims.claim: A void before a reservation leaves a look held. It is released (as a spurious fault) when the judge process dies.
claims.analyst: POLISH: needs a void racing a judge's start (coverage_judge is the only reserve caller); it heals itself
claims.page_rule_why: rare: a void in a judge's own second (DNS hand-command-in-a-run's-own-second)

claims.claim: Re-holding a mod on the same day with new words is not imported into the store.
claims.analyst: POLISH / near NOT-A-BUG: `import_live` runs only at `init --import` (cutover), and every reader (`mod_owner_hold.load`) honours the file row with the new words anyway
claims.page_rule_why: a new hold with new words is his ordinary input; his-hold-refuses-launch "with his words"; fixed a6aac8a6fc, t_his_hold_refuses_launch

claims.claim: `doctor` says OK after a failed integrity check.
claims.analyst: POLISH: needs a corrupt store
claims.page_rule_why: a corrupt store is an unreadable store, the failure probe-never-lies names; doctor said OK; fixed 9a8593dc91

claims.claim: `pipe off` says "no run is live" when its follow-up read failed.
claims.analyst: POLISH: needs a read failure right after a successful write
claims.page_rule_why: an unreadable store on pipe off's follow-up read is probe-never-lies' own failure, met alone; fixed 9a8593dc91

claims.claim: The "stage advanced on a voided run" flag matches run ids by substring (rm-probe-1 inside rm-probe-10).
claims.analyst: POLISH: a wrong FLAG line in a report, with no gate. Note that be673ed895's `run_X~2` ids make a prefix collision possible on a re-admitted unit.
claims.page_rule_why: run ids rm-probe-1 and rm-probe-10 are ordinary; void-never-moves-a-stage "flags no other run"; fixed a6aac8a6fc, t_void_never_moves_a_stage

claims.claim: The per-verb p95 estimator lets one slow call in five pass.
claims.analyst: POLISH: test strength
claims.page_rule_why: the page promises each verb's own 95th percentile; an estimator that passes one slow call in five reads about the 80th, so the gate is wrong and no test goes red (blind relabel 2026-11-25, 65%)

claims.claim: Round three's new tests can pass while the behaviour they advertise fails (exit 4 is untested; thread exceptions are not collected).
claims.analyst: POLISH: test strength
claims.page_rule_why: polish: test strength with no broken component described
